1.note: Literally "who decrees with his speech, and none brings". Read as: no one can bring an answer or a rival word. The sense is uncertain.

2.note: Isa 32:5 sets the נָבָל (villain, churl) and the כִּילַי (miser) against the נָדִיב (generous man). So Villainy is the companion, and later the parent, of Miserliness.

3.note: Literally "for there their inclination dwells, dread". The sense is uncertain; עָרֶץ may echo the rhyme with אֶרֶץ in the next line.

4.note: As in the introduction: Isa 47:8 calls Babylon עֲדִינָה, "the voluptuous one". Medieval Hebrew writers use the name for Baghdad. Here it is the capital of the Jews of the East.

5.note: No-Amon (Nah 3:8) is Thebes in Egypt; medieval Jewish writers often take it as Alexandria. With Elam, it marks the limits of the East from west to east.

6.note: "The Glorious Land" (Dan 11:16, 41), that is, the Land of Israel. צְבִי also means "gazelle"; the poem of its hosts plays on both senses.

7.he: נַחְנוּ בְנֵי הֶבֶל פְּאֵר תֵּבֵל / יָמִים תְּהִלּוֹתָם יְרַנֵּנוּ
7.note: הֶבֶל is Abel, but also "vanity, breath": the boast can be read as "we are sons of vanity", a joke at the miser's party. יָמִים can be "seas" or "days" ("the days sing their praises").

8.note: "Our clouds" are probably the clouds of dust, or of arrows, that the army raises: the sky learns from them to rain blood. Uncertain.

9.note: A pun: Haran (חָרָן) and "wrath" (חָרוֹן). The merchants (רוֹכְלֵי) of Haran come from Ezek 27:23.

10.note: A pun on מוֹנֶה, which in line 385 means "oppressor" (from יָנָה) and here, in the words of Jer 33:13, means "one who counts" (the shepherd counting his flock).

11.note: A pun: "the wrath (חֲמַת) of the men of Hamath (חֲמָת)". At the end of the line, קְרָבוֹת (battles) rhymes with קְרָבִים (inward parts).

12.note: נִתְעַל is read from נַעַל, "we shoe ourselves", that is, we put on armor. The form is unusual and chosen for the rhyme with עָל and מָעַל.

13.note: The poem rhymes on צְבִי in three senses: the Glorious Land (Land of Israel), the gazelle, and glory ("all glory is gone"). Compare m. Avot 5:20, "swift as a gazelle, mighty as a lion".

14.note: "Their foes" are the communities, the foes of the generous, who prevailed over the generous. The subject changes without warning in the Hebrew.

15.note: הַשְּׁדוּדָה is from Ps 137:8, בַּת בָּבֶל הַשְּׁדוּדָה, "daughter of Babylon, who is to be destroyed". The kingdom of Miserliness began in Babel.
